tried: Warm-start spyder_walk_v3's actor and critic into SpyderDesert-v0 and fine-tune
outcome: The gait was destroyed within a few thousand steps (ep_rew_mean 6331 -> 146) and never recovered; the run settled at 0.37 m/s, below the do-nothing control
do_not_repeat_unless: the critic is reset AND the replay buffer can be relabelled under the new reward — which needs world x,y in the observation, which it is not

guard.why: Nothing on disk records that a run was warm-started. config.json has no 'initialized_from' field and no reference to a parent checkpoint, so a warm-started run and a from-scratch run are byte-identical in the record. learnings/002 already states this in its own `guard:` field. No schema on nulls.jsonl fixes it -- the missing fact is upstream, in what train.py writes.

tried: Train the hound on HoundDesert-v0 from scratch with the flat-tuned reward (ctrl_cost_weight 0.1)
outcome: Zero action scored 961 against the trained policy's 109 — doing nothing was 9x better. Reproduced the spider's failure on a different body with no warm-start, isolating the reward as the sole cause
do_not_repeat_unless: ctrl_cost_weight is lowered to 0.02 and the forward term is replaced by command tracking, per CORE_PLAN.md

guard.note: The term is named forward_velocity, not forward -- checked against runs/hound_pd_desert_s1/config.json rather than guessed. A guessed name would have made every clause vacuously true and the guard permanently green.

tried: Regenerate the desert heightfield at GRID=2048 (3.906 cm cells, ~4 cells per 8.5 cm wheel radius) to remove the hound's passive backward creep, as proposed in robots/hound/build.py, ROADMAP.md:46, research/CORE_PLAN.md:317 and learnings/005:52
outcome: Does not work, and the mechanism it targets is not present. Creep is -1.7761 +/- 0.0276 m at GRID=1024 and -1.7641 +/- 0.0066 m at GRID=2048, a paired difference of +11.99 +/- 26.18 mm over 20 seeds = 0.675% of the +1776 mm a fix would require. The spawn pad is exactly flat (max|h| and peak-to-peak both 0.000e+00 over 3212 cells within 2.5 m) and every contact across 40 episodes landed within 2.034 m, so the two-disagreeing-prism-normals mechanism was never available where the creep is generated
cost: ~2 CPU-minutes to measure. Would have cost a full re-measurement of every terrain-specific number in the record, since the regenerated desert correlates with the committed one at only +0.061
do_not_repeat_unless: the goal is contact fidelity for a policy that DRIVES off the flat pad onto real slope -- which is untested and may be a real effect -- and never as a creep fix; or guards/spawn_pad.py fails, meaning the pad is no longer exactly flat and the mechanism has become available

guard.why: The release condition is about the INTENT of a terrain regeneration ('the goal is contact fidelity for a policy that drives off the flat pad onto real slope') and about another guard's state (spawn_pad failing). Neither appears in a run's config.json. The terrain_spec hash records WHICH ground a run used, but using a regenerated desert is not itself the dead end -- the dead end was regenerating it AS A CREEP FIX, and intent is not a field.
